`using` (TS 5.2) declares a resource that is disposed automatically when the scope exits, by calling its `[Symbol.dispose]()` method, even on early return or throw; `await using` does the same with `Symbol.asyncDispose`. Multiple `using` declarations are disposed in reverse order, and you need a tsconfig lib/target that includes the disposable types plus runtime support for Symbol.dispose, so I'd check the Node version we run before relying on it. Action: I can show a small example, such as wrapping a DB connection, if you want; no file changes needed.

`structuredClone` deep-copies with the structured clone algorithm: it keeps Dates, Maps, Sets, typed arrays, undefined values and circular references, while the JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, drops undefined and functions, empties Maps and Sets, and throws on cycles. Both lose class prototypes, and structuredClone throws on functions. So the reviewer was probably right to flag the JSON version unless the data is plain JSON. Action: I can look at the flagged line in the PR and say which one it should use.

They're not the same. HTTP/1.1 keep-alive only reuses a TCP connection for sequential requests, so one request has to finish before the next starts on that connection (browsers open several connections to compensate). HTTP/2 multiplexing interleaves many request/response streams as frames on a single connection, which removes that head-of-line wait at the HTTP layer, though TCP-level loss can still stall all streams. Action: none needed in the repo; I can put a two-line version together for standup if useful.

tsx uses esbuild to strip types and run the file, so it starts fast but does no type-checking, and it handles ESM, CommonJS and tsconfig paths with little setup. ts-node uses the real TypeScript compiler, so it type-checks as it goes, which is slower, and its ESM support has needed loader flags. In practice use tsx for running scripts and keep `tsc --noEmit` in CI for type errors. Action: nothing to change in the repo; the tsx dev dependency is already added, and the lockfile still needs an install.
